text: i would raise the max draws up a ladder since we will hit it very quick once the density starts packing in
resolution: Raised the streaming per-frame draw cap MAX_DRAWS from 4096 to 16384 in framework/world/streaming.zig, per the user's call that dense maps will hit it fast: contiguous-only merging (the req_0537 correctness fix) fragments ranges more by design, and every material family multiplies them. Cost is trivial — the Draw scratch is 16 bytes/draw and small worlds allocate min(actual-need, cap) regardless; only dense massive worlds touch the new ceiling (worst-case loader node reserve ~13MB on the 124k-chunk lab). Documented the REAL ceilings beyond this constant in the comment: gpu/3d.zig's per-scene mesh collection (MAX_SCENE_MESHES=32768 children) and per-frame command-encode cost — if the warn-once dropped-draws log ever fires at 16384, the right next move is distance-priority eviction of far LOD ranges, not a bigger number. Unit tests 4/4 green, loader rebuilt, 512-block lab verified unchanged (213 draws, no cap warning).
